  "text": "Tobias came back by the church road in the morning because it was the only road there was.\n\nThe tide was where a tide should be. Gulls were out over the point, quarrelling. There was wind enough to lift the collar of his coat. He counted the posts from the top of the dune and got eleven, and then counted again and got eleven, and could not have said why that steadied him.\n\nThe house stood where it had always stood. The door was shut. He went up the twenty steps of path with his hand on the rope rail and did not hurry, and when he reached the porch he did not knock, because there was no one to knock for. He knew that the way he knew weather.\n\nThe front room was dark. The lamp stood on the sill unlit, the chip in its base turned to the glass as she always kept it. The rug lay square on the boards. There was sand on it, a little, in the shape of two feet set side by side, facing the window.\n\nHe did not go in. He stood on the step and looked at the sea through her room, the way she must have looked at it, and the sea looked back the way it always had, flat and grey and not interested.\n\nAfter a while he went down.
